newsitem.title: CANADA: Aerospace firms vie for big Canada contract.
newsitem.headline: Aerospace firms vie for big Canada contract.

text.p: Aerospace companies from around the world are vying for a chance to win a C$600 million (US$434 million) contract to build 15 search and rescue helicopters for the Canadian government.

Four international consortiums have launched intense lobbying campaigns as the Canadian government evaluates their bids to build a fleet of helicopters to replace rickety Labrador choppers bought in the 1960s.
"It's going through a rigorous evaluation, I can tell you that," Defence Minister Art Eggleton told reporters on Thursday. "We hope to have a decision in the fall."
Ottawa has set aside up to C$600 million (US$$434 million) for 15 new helicopters, but Eggleton said he would consider job creation and quality as well as price.

The four teams competing for the contract have assembled proposals that seem to solve almost every Canadian economic problem -- unemployment, uneven regional development and the lack of start-up capital for small businesses.

United Technologies Corp.'s Sikorsky Aircraft Division is offering massive job creation, the participation of more than 20 Canadian companies, development in some of Canada's less developed regions, a venture capital fund for small high-tech firms and "the lowest price on the table."
The Connecticut company has even given its proposed helicopter a Canadian name: the Maplehawk, modelled after Sikorsky's Blackhawk.

A second consortium, Team Cormorant, led by GKN Westland of Britain and its Italian partner Finmeccanica unit Agusta, has also promised jobs. The group is holding out C$30 million (US$22 million) in spinoffs for Quebec aerospace companies, and a price that will "provide the best value" for the Canadian government.
"We are significantly under that (C$600 million) number," Frank Bamford, Canadian spokesman for Westland, said in an interview this week.
Westland and Agusta have teamed up with Canadian companies Bombardier Inc., Magellan Aerospace Corp. and a long list of other Canadian and international companies.

But the Westland-Agusta team needs to live down a turbulent history in Canada. Westland won a previous C$5.8 billion (US$4.2 billion) contract to build search and rescue helicopters for Canada's Conservative government, which was voted out of office in 1993.
The winning Liberals, who are still in power, cancelled the contract after the price tag outraged Canadians. The Liberal government paid a C$159 million (US$115 million) penalty to cancel the deal.
Officials from Boeing Co. of Seattle are promoting a bid that promises jobs and business spinoffs for the Canadian economy.

Eurocopter, a merger of the helicopter divisions of Aerospatiale of France and Daimler-Benz of Germany, is offering a long-term commitment to employment and a multitude of contracts for Canadian firms if it wins the bid with its Cougar helicopter.
Eurocopter has teamed up with Canada's SNC-Lavalin Group Inc. and Spar Aerospace Ltd.
